lesson_title: Defining Quadrilaterals by Sides and Angles
hook_text: Same four sides. Different shape. What did the gate lose?
clip_script:
A farm gate is made as a rectangle: two long rails of 3 metres, two short uprights of 1,2 metres, bolted at the corners. When it is new and hung, every corner is a right angle, the rails are parallel, the uprights are parallel. A rectangle, by definition: a parallelogram with a right angle.

After a season the far end drops. The bolts hold, so the four sides are the same lengths as before, but the corners have turned: two are now about 80 degrees and two about 100. The rails are still parallel, the uprights are still parallel. Both pairs of opposite sides parallel: a parallelogram. It lost its right angles, so it is no longer a rectangle. A push removes angles and keeps parallel sides, and the definitions track exactly that.
visual_style: A rectangular farm gate leaning slowly into a parallelogram, its corner squares fading while the parallel arrowheads stay lit; a diagonal brace snaps it back
